subject: Multi-year prepay structure & payment terms discussion
messages:

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>

Subject: Intro + Multi-year prepay options for predictable economics

Hi Ellen / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, I wanted to put some concrete options on the table for a multi-year prepay that balances cost savings with your cashflow constraints. High level thoughts: 

- 3-year vs 1-year: deeper discount for 3-year committed prepay (example: 20% effective vs 8–10% for annual).
- Ramp schedule: front-loaded consumption assumptions often cause large initial spend; we recommend a staged ramp (Year1=40%, Year2=35%, Year3=25%) to align unit economics and headcount growth.
- Payment terms: we can offer Net 60 on the committed prepay balance for enterprise customers, or Net 30 for shorter terms; partial upfront is possible for larger discounts.

Would love to get your constraints (preferred term length, whether you require Net 60/90, and whether a milestone schedule tied to product rollout would be acceptable). I’m copying Marcus (pricing) and Ava (finance liaison) to draft a formal term sheet once we have your preferences.

Next step: if you can share the Procurement team's preferred payment window and whether CloudFin requires milestones for recognition, we’ll send a proposed term sheet and ramp schedule by next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Hi Connor —

Thanks for the summary — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

1) Preferred term: Procurement is inclined toward a 2- to 3-year commitment if the economics are compelling.
2) Payment terms: standard for CloudFin is Net 60 for platform vendors, but exceptions to Net 90 are handled on a case-by-case basis.
3) Milestones: Procurement prefers partial upfront + milestone-based draws tied to expansion/Go-Live (we typically do 30% upfront, 40% at production, 30% at adoption milestone).

Before we proceed, finance wants to understand: how much additional discount is tied to a partial upfront vs full prepay? Also, if we go with a ramp schedule, can you provide an example amortization and invoice cadence?

Ellen Park
Head of Strategic Procurement, CloudFin
ellen@cloudfin.com

Connor —

Drafting some numbers to reply to CloudFin. Key points to include:

- Discount bands (ballpark): 12% off list for 1-year full prepay; 18% for 2-year prepay; 24% for 3-year prepay. These assume a standard ramp; we can increase ~3–5% if CloudFin agrees to a larger upfront (50% upfront).
- Ramp amortization example (2-year, $1.2M list annualized): Year1 invoice schedule = 50% upfront, then quarterly invoices for usage true-up; Year2 = quarterly. Alternatively if they require Net 60 on the prepaid invoices we can invoice at signing with Net 60.
- Milestone schedule: map 30/40/30 to delivery milestones. We should confirm which events CloudFin considers 'Go-Live' and 'Adoption'.
- Risk: longer Net terms (Net 90) increase our AR exposure; need finance sign-off for Net 90.

I'll attach a quick term sheet and a sample Excel ramp that shows cashflow & discount sensitivity. Connor, suggest we propose two formal options to Ellen: (A) 2-year prepay, 30% upfront, Net 60 on invoices; (B) 3-year prepay, 50% upfront, extended discount but Net 30 on upfront invoice (finance would prefer shorter receivable on big upfronts).

-Marcus
Marcus Lin

Ellen —

Thanks for the details. Attaching a proposed term sheet and a sample ramp schedule for CloudFin (see attachments: Redwood-TermSheet-DF-2026-0047.pdf, CF-Prepay-RampSchedule.xlsx). Highlights: 

Option A — 2-year prepay (recommended for balance)
- Total committed value: $2,400,000 list over 2 years
- Effective discount: 18% off list
- Payment schedule: 30% upfront at signing (invoice Net 60), 40% at production (invoice Net 60), remainder quarterly true-ups.
- Ramp assumption: Year1 consumption = 55%, Year2 = 45%

Option B — 3-year deeper discount
- Total committed value: $3,600,000 list over 3 years
- Effective discount: 24% off list (or +4% if 50% upfront)
- Payment schedule: 50% upfront at signing (invoice Net 30), 25% at production, 25% at Year2 anniversary.

Notes on terms & exceptions:
- Net 60 is acceptable for the majority of invoices; Net 90 requires finance approval and a credit assessment.
- Milestone payments are supported; we recommend mapping to signatory milestones rather than internal adoption metrics to avoid disputes.
- Early termination: refunds on prepay are handled per schedule — typically pro rata less a termination fee; full details in term sheet.

If CloudFin agrees to Option A, we'll issue the redlined term sheet and coordinate a Procure-to-Pay PO flow. If they prefer Option B with 50% upfront, Laura can start the finance credit check and get sign-off for Net 30 on the upfront invoice.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Finance Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Redwood-TermSheet-DF-2026-0047.pdf, CF-Prepay-RampSchedule.xlsx

Ava / Connor —

Appreciate the clear options and the sample schedule. CloudFin's internal stakeholders prefer Option A (2-year) but with milestone-based invoicing to smooth cashflow as follows: 30% upfront at signing (we would ask for Net 60 on that invoice), 40% at production (Net 60), 30% at 12-month adoption milestone (Net 60). The procurement team will not accept Net 30 on the upfront.

We also want to confirm that the 18% discount is fixed for the term and that any overages beyond committed consumption are billed at the discounted rate, not list. Please confirm in the redline.

If Redwood can accept Net 60 on all three invoices, CloudFin will issue a PO within 7 business days and proceed with the initial payment. We'll route the PO to your finance mailbox and include our standard milestone definitions in the PO.

Ellen Park
Head of Strategic Procurement, CloudFin
